out.other_title: Does debate still work when judges hold strong inaccurate priors or cognitive biases?
out.rationale: The authors cite prior work showing effectiveness even with unreliable experts [30, 31, 36], including Michael et al. [36], say that prior work largely ignores scenarios where judges exhibit cognitive biases or hold strong prior beliefs, and state that their work addresses this limitation by investigating whether debate remains effective when judges have existing cognitive biases about controversial topics. Michael et al. list cognitive biases and strong priors as an open problem, saying human judges should be evaluated and trained on questions where they have strong inaccurate priors, so the source ADDRESSES the target's open question.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: Whether debate remains effective when judges hold cognitive biases or strong prior beliefs about controversial topics; tested with human judges of varying prior beliefs and with LLM judges with and without simulated personas
